title: ACE Inhibitors vs ARBs vs ARNI

questions.stem: A patient started lisinopril 2 months ago and now has a dry, tickly cough that will not go away. What is the best change?

options.text: Keep lisinopril and add a cough syrup

questions.explanation: D is correct: the cough comes from bradykinin, and angiotensin receptor blockers like losartan do not raise bradykinin, so cough is much less common. A is wrong because enalapril is another ACE inhibitor, and the cough is a class effect. C keeps the drug that causes the cough. B leaves the blood pressure untreated when a good alternative exists.

questions.stem: Why do ACE inhibitors cause a dry cough?

options.text: They block the angiotensin II receptor
Bradykinin is no longer broken down and builds up

questions.explanation: C is correct: the ACE enzyme also breaks down bradykinin, so blocking it lets bradykinin build up and cause cough. A describes angiotensin receptor blockers, which rarely cause cough. B is a real effect, but it causes heart rhythm risk, not cough. D is wrong because ACE inhibitors lower aldosterone, not raise it.

questions.stem: A patient on lisinopril arrives with swelling of the lips and tongue. What is the best plan for lisinopril?

options.text: Stop it and never restart it

questions.explanation: D is correct: this is angioedema, which can block the airway, so stop the drug and never restart it. A still exposes the patient to the drug. B is another ACE inhibitor with the same bradykinin effect. C keeps the drug that caused the swelling.

questions.stem: A patient with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction takes enalapril and is switching to sacubitril-valsartan. When can the first sacubitril-valsartan dose be given?

options.text: 12 hours after the last enalapril dose
36 hours after the last enalapril dose
7 days after the last enalapril dose

questions.explanation: C is correct: stop the ACE inhibitor and wait 36 hours, because overlapping neprilysin blocking and ACE blocking raises angioedema risk. A and B are too soon and allow that overlap. D waits longer than needed and leaves the heart failure undertreated.

questions.stem: Which of these should be avoided? Select all that apply.

options.text: Combining an ACE inhibitor with an angiotensin receptor blocker
Switching to losartan after an ACE inhibitor cough
Continuing an angiotensin receptor blocker after pregnancy is found
Adding aliskiren to an ACE inhibitor in a patient with diabetes
Sacubitril-valsartan in a patient who had angioedema from an ACE inhibitor

questions.explanation: A, C, D, and E are correct: never combine an ACE inhibitor and an angiotensin receptor blocker, stop these drugs when pregnancy is found (boxed warning), never add aliskiren in diabetes, and never use sacubitril-valsartan after angioedema from an ACE inhibitor. B is the recommended switch for an ACE inhibitor cough, so it should not be avoided.

questions.stem: Two weeks after lisinopril is started, a patient's creatinine rises from 1.0 to 1.15 mg/dL. Potassium is normal. What is the best action?

options.text: Double the lisinopril dose to protect the kidney

questions.explanation: A is correct: a 15% rise is expected because filtration pressure drops; a rise of more than 30% needs a closer look. B stops a helpful drug for an expected change. C is wrong because an ACE inhibitor and an angiotensin receptor blocker should never be combined. D raises the dose in response to a lab check, which can push creatinine and potassium higher.

questions.stem: After starting or raising the dose of an ACE inhibitor, when should creatinine and potassium be checked?

options.text: In 6 months with the lipid panel

questions.explanation: D is correct: check creatinine and potassium within 2 to 4 weeks of starting or raising the dose. A waits for symptoms, which can miss high potassium before it causes heart rhythm problems. B and C wait far too long to catch an early rise.

questions.stem: Why does potassium tend to rise on ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers?

options.text: Less aldosterone, so the kidney keeps potassium
More bradykinin pulls potassium into the blood

questions.explanation: A is correct: less aldosterone means the kidney keeps potassium. B is wrong because bradykinin explains cough and angioedema, not potassium. C is wrong because these drugs do not contain potassium. D is the opposite of what happens: filtration pressure drops.

questions.stem: Which statements about sacubitril-valsartan are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: It can be combined with an ACE inhibitor at lower doses
Valsartan blocks the angiotensin II receptor
It is used for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
Blocking neprilysin raises angioedema risk because neprilysin breaks down bradykinin

questions.explanation: B, C, D, and E are correct: sacubitril blocks neprilysin, valsartan blocks the receptor, the drug is for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, and blocking neprilysin raises angioedema risk. A is wrong because it can never be taken with an ACE inhibitor at any dose.

questions.stem: Which drug is an angiotensin receptor blocker?
questions.explanation: A is correct: angiotensin receptor blockers end in sartan, like losartan and valsartan. B and D end in pril, so they are ACE inhibitors. C, aliskiren, is a different drug that must never be added to these drugs in diabetes.
